articles.title: 'Not a close case': Judge orders FCC to halt review of ABC's broadcast licenses
articles.summary: A judge ordered FCC Chairman Brendan Carr to halt its early review of ABC's broadcasting licenses. A federal judge ordered Wednesday that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) halt its early review of broadcasting licenses of eight ABC stations as part of the agency's intense feud with the Disney-owned network. U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan ruled in favor of ABC, which sued the FCC on First Amendment grounds after the agency announced it was moving up the license renewals of eight stations owned by the network years ahead of schedule. "This is not a close case," AliKhan wrote in the ruling. "Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration," an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital . Disney Sues Fcc Over ‘Retaliatory Campaign Against Abc,’ Seeks To Block Early Renewal Proceedings An ABC News spokesperson called the ruling an "important victory for the First Amendment." "While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear," an FCC spokesperson said in a statement. "The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations." Read On The Fox News App FCC Chairman Brendan Carr had called for early renewal of eight ABC-owned stations' licenses in April. The licenses were originally scheduled to be renewed between 2028 and 2031. KFSN-TV in Fresno, KABC-TV in Los Angeles, KGO-TV in San Francisco, WLS-TV in Chicago, WABC-TV in New York, WTVD in North Carolina, WPVI-TV in Philadelphia and KTRK-TV in Houston were the stations named by the FCC. Fcc Boss Brendan Carr Maintains Early Abc License Renewal Is About Dei Probe, Not Jimmy Kimmel Controversy While the FCC maintained the license crackdown was focused on the legality of Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices, Carr's announcement came as tensions reignited between President Donald Trump and ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel. Kimmel had quipped that first lady Melania Trump had the glow of an "expectant widow" on his show, a joke made days before a gunman targeted members of the Trump administration at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner but caught national attention after the assassination attempt. Both the first lady and President Trump called for ABC to take action against Kimmel at the time. Carr had previously leveled a thinly veiled threat against Disney last year over controversial remarks Kimmel made about the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. 'The View' Eased Up On Political Candidate Bookings Amid Fcc Inquiry, Report Says ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr have had an intense feud during the second Trump administration. The FCC separately launched a probe into ABC's daytime talk show "The View" in an effort to upend its status as a bona fide news program, which exempts the network from abiding by long-standing rules requiring equal time for political candidates. In previous court filings, ABC claimed that the actions taken by the FCC had a chilling effect on the network's free speech, pointing to how "The View" has refrained from inviting political candidates onto the show as a result of the crackdown. articles.title: Trump pushed to reinstate Nvidia's CEO while owning millions in company stock
articles.summary: President Trump holds tens of millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride over the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show. Mr. Trump stood to lose large sums with CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure, and stood to profit handsomely after he successfully pressed the chip developer's board to reinstate Huang. Nvidia stock surged more than 30% when Huang returned to the company on Monday, reversing a weekslong slide. Huang resigned two weeks ago over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who ran a company accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China, and another alleged affair with a subordinate. Mr. Trump said Monday he personally spoke with Nvidia's board and "convinced them" to rehire Huang, offering an "assurance" that there was no national security threat. Mr. Trump held between $13 million and $58 million in Nvidia stock in his investment accounts as of the end of 2025, according to financial disclosures filed with the Office of Government Ethics. He bought or sold the company's stock in more than 100 transactions that were worth between $27 million and nearly $98 million between January 2025 and September 2026. The value of the president's Nvidia shares increased anywhere from $1.3 million to $14.8 million on Monday, before paring back some of those gains when Nvidia's share price ticked down Tuesday. The range is so large because it isn't clear how many shares of Nvidia the president currently owns, but it can be roughly estimated based on his sales and purchases this year. "President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions," a White House spokesman told CBS News Tuesday, adding that his investments mirror indexes like the Schwab 1000. "Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers." In addition to the president, several of his appointees to positions in the State, Commerce and Treasury departments as well as the IRS reported millions in Nvidia stock in their investment portfolios. Many have since sold their holdings. Forbes estimates Mr. Trump's net worth at more than $6 billion, making Nvidia a small part of his total wealth. And Nvidia is one of the world's most valuable public companies, at more than $3.7 trillion, so many investors hold shares in the tech giant. Still, some ethics experts questioned Mr. Trump's large stake in Nvidia, especially after he intervened to boost the company's fortunes. "This goes beyond a conflict of interest," said Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "He is squarely, explicitly using his power as president to benefit himself financially. He has prioritized his finances over the security of the nation." Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit government watchdog, told CBS News that Mr. Trump's "continued ownership of stock in this company is the clearest example of how the president's personal financial interest makes everything he does suspect." Mr. Trump's personal investments have drawn controversy in the past, including his stakes in publicly traded energy companies, firms that have business with the government and his family's cryptocurrency firm . He has denied any conflict of interest. Some critics called for legal reforms to prohibit the president and members of Congress from buying and selling stocks while they hold office. Elected officials are generally allowed to trade individual stocks, though lawmakers from both parties have called for the practice to be banned. Richard Painter, a law professor at the University of Minnesota and former chief ethics attorney for the White House between 2005 and 2007, said he has long argued for changes to the federal conflict of interest law that prohibits government employees from participating in matters that result in their personal enrichment while in office. That current law does not apply to the president, vice president or members of Congress, he said. "We need a prohibition on this right away," he said, adding that the new Congress may take up the cause in January. Painter called Mr. Trump's intervention with the Nvidia board "a huge conflict of interest" and overreach of government power. "It's not the job of the government to call up and say who the CEO of a company should be," he told CBS News. The president has defended his decision to intervene , saying on CNBC that "we have to protect our geniuses" and arguing that Nvidia — as the world's leading designer of advanced chips — plays a key role in maintaining the U.S.' lead over China in AI technology. Mr. Trump has also frequently pointed to the performance of the stock market as a barometer of his success as president. Shortly after Huang was reinstated, Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal the "response from the market has been very positive," and "that really shows the decision was right." Beyond Mr. Trump, numerous political appointees held Nvidia stock. Some divested themselves of their holdings after they were appointed to government positions, federal filings show. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin owned between $250,000 and $500,000 in Nvidia stock in March 2026, and sold $500,000 to $1 million in shares of the tech company in June of this year, his financial disclosures show. "As Secretary of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin acts to ensure full compliance with all ethics and conflict of interest rules," said a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security. In the Commerce Department, where Secretary Howard Lutnick is facing scrutiny over whether he has done enough to crack down on highly sensitive AI chip sales to China, a number of senior advisers last year reported selling large positions in Nvidia. Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm that was previously run by Lutnick and is now controlled by his sons, reported holding roughly 1 million shares of Nvidia for its clients as of Sept. 30, worth around $228 million at the time. Those shares were worth just over $150 million at Tuesday's price. None of Lutnick's personal financial disclosures filed by the federal government mention Nvidia holdings or transactions. In the State Department, some of Mr. Trump's diplomatic appointees had Nvidia holdings. Charles Kushner, the U.S. ambassador to France and father of Mr. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, reported Nvidia holdings totaling between $1.5 million and $6 million, according to public disclosures filed January 2025. U.S. Ambassador to Costa Rica Melinda Hildebrand reported Nvidia holdings between $5 million and $25 million, her April 2025  disclosures show. The Texas billionaire, who was a major Trump campaign fundraiser, sold the stock in November of that same year, filings show. Warren Stephens, another major Trump donor and ambassador to the United Kingdom, reported Nvidia holdings between $750,000 and $1.5 million, according to his January 2025  disclosures. He sold those shares in July and August 2025, a few months after he was sworn in as ambassador. In the Treasury Department, when she was nominated to be under secretary for International Affairs, Erin Browne held Nvidia shares totaling between $250,000 and $500,000, her disclosures from January show. Browne sold the stock before her confirmation in August, filings show. Todd Newnam, who was appointed chief financial officer of the IRS in January, holds between $115,000 and $250,000 in Nvidia stock, according to his financial disclosure, filed in April of last year. Newnam, a former CEO of a tech company, was part of the Department of Government Efficiency team that sought to streamline government spending and cut the federal workforce. "All OGE (Office of Government Ethics) 278 filers are required to disclose any equity positions they hold and are advised of their recusal obligations in accordance with the ethics rules," an IRS spokesperson said Tuesday, referring to the financial disclosure required by members of the executive branch of the federal government. Many other officials could be indirectly exposed to Nvidia stock if they invested in mutual funds or similar assets. For example, Vice President JD Vance reported $1 million to $5 million in a fund that tracks the S&P 500 — and Nvidia is one of that index's largest components. articles.title: FedEx aircraft overruns runway at Miami airport, closing all but one runway
articles.summary: A FedEx airplane overran a runway at the Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, forcing all but one runway to temporarily close the day before Thanksgiving, according to officials. There were no reports of injuries after the plane ran off the runway at about 8:40 p.m., the airport reported. The incident happened almost three months after an Amazon cargo jet overshot another runway in Miami, killing five people on the ground. By early Thursday, the Federal Aviation Administration was reporting hourslong flight delays. The FAA, which is investigating, said the McDonnell Douglas MD-11 was coming from Memphis. FedEx said the plane had “an issue upon landing” and that it is coordinating with investigating officials. “We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries,” the company said in a statement. FedEx had just started flying MD-11s again in May to deliver packages after that type of plane crashed in Kentucky last year as it was taking off. The UPS plane's left engine flew off and three pilots along with 12 people on the ground were killed. The FAA had approved Boeing’s proposed fix for the MD-11s “after extensive review.” The airport recommended that passengers scheduled to fly Wednesday night should check with their airlines for the latest flight updates before traveling to the airport. “We appreciate our passengers’ patience as we work to safely resume normal operations,” the airport said in a statement. The runway this FedEx plane landed on Wednesday is different than the one the Amazon cargo plane overran in September. But three of Miami’s runways converge at the west end, so the FedEx plane ended up close to where the Amazon plane careened across a road and struck a van filled with a plane cleaning crew. The incident also comes less than two weeks after a minor collision between two planes at a taxiway intersection at the Miami airport. The wing of the Copa flight and the nose of the UPS plane collided. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the incident Wednesday. The National Transportation Safety Board said it had no information about the situation. ___ AP Transportation Writer Josh Funk contributed. articles.title: A man in Boston won $1 million in the lottery. Then ICE arrested him.
articles.summary: ICE in Boston arrested Ariel Velasquez-Morales, an undocumented migrant from El Salvador who won $1 million in the Massachusetts Lottery last week. - DHS Over the weekend, the Massachusetts Lottery shared a picture of Ariel Velasquez-Morales smiling gently as he gripped an oversized check for $1 million in winnings. On social media, commenters congratulated him, with one person writing they hoped he would be able to “make any dreams come true.” But Velasquez-Morales was arrested Tuesday by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in East Boston, the same neighborhood where he bought the $10 winning scratch-off ticket from a local market. He now faces deportation as ICE says the Salvadoran national has been in the country illegally for more than a decade. “Looks like his luck ran out,” said ICE Assistant Director of Public Affairs Micah Bock in a release announcing the arrest. It is unclear whether the publication of his lottery winnings attracted ICE’s attention. ICE declined to answer questions from CNN about what led to the arrest or where Velasquez-Morales is being detained. Velasquez-Morales illegally entered the United States in 2013, during the Obama administration, in the Rio Grande Valley in Texas. Border Patrol agents issued him a notice to appear before an immigration judge, and he was released into the country with a list of free legal service providers, the agency said. “A Department of Justice immigration judge ordered Velasquez-Morales removed in 2014, but he illegally remained in the country,” the ICE release said. He will remain in ICE custody pending his removal from the US. CNN has been unable to determine whether he has legal representation. President Donald Trump has overseen a massive immigration crackdown after promising to lead the largest deportation operation in US history. In his second term, arrests have shifted away from the border and focused more on the interior of the country, where aggressive tactics have become a hallmark of ICE’s ramped-up detention efforts. By July 2026, there were nearly 66,000 detainees in ICE custody, an increase of nearly 70% from the total detained when Trump took office the year prior. But after a Republican wipeout in the midterms, Trump has publicly questioned whether the tactics were too hard-line and unpopular. It remains to be seen, though, whether he is considering significant changes to his immigration policies. “Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the United States and will be removed as quickly as possible,” ICE said in its release on Velasquez-Morales. “Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin’s leadership, ICE is delivering on its mission to enforce our nation’s immigration laws, restore accountability and protect American communities.” Velasquez-Morales was playing the lottery’s “ $2,000,000 50X Cashword ,” in which players scratch cards resembling crossword puzzles to try to reveal complete words. It was the first puzzle he had scratched, the lottery said, and he matched 11 words. He chose to accept his winnings in cash, which would give him a one-time lump sum of $650,000 before taxes, according to ICE. It is not clear what will happen to his winnings. Massachusetts lottery participants do not need to be legal residents of the state to play, but they must be 21 or older and be located in the state at the time they purchase or play. CNN has sought comment from the Massachusetts State Lottery Commission. articles.title: Pier collapses, seawalls breached, homes flooded as king tides thrash California
articles.summary: A wave crashes over a breakwater Wednesday as high surf and tides hit Pacifica, south of San Francisco. (Noah Berger / Associated Press) Coastal California communities were deluged Wednesday by powerful waves and record-breaking high tides, breaching seawalls, flooding some homes and causing a chunk of a pier south of San Francisco to collapse amid 20- to 30-foot waves. The damage was greatest in the coastal town of Pacifica, where relentless waves sent water streaming down several city blocks and collapsed a section of the historic pier. A massive swell of ocean water struck the perpendicular  portion of the L-shaped pier, causing the vertical supports to suddenly buckle. King tides — fueled by a historic El Niño , record hot ocean temperatures and strong swells coming from the west — set all-time high tide levels in parts of Southern California, flooding multiple homes in Orange County. “This El Niño is unprecedented with its strength,” said San Mateo County Supervisor Ray Mueller. “For this to be happening when it is a beautiful day on the coastside today, in clear sunshine and no wind, is really significant.” As salt water poured over carefully-lined rows of sandbags and inundated multiple homes in Pacifica — where floodwaters were knee-high on some streets by midday — Mueller told The Times that pumps that were supposed to remove floodwaters were all operational, but overwhelmed by the amount of water coming over the seawall. “They’re having a hard time keeping up with the water that’s coming over,” Mueller said, noting that local officials will need help with the recovery. “We really are going to need resources to shore up this entire area. And frankly, these pumps are going to need to be fixed as well, so that they’re operating better.” Waves pound the Pacifica Municipal Pier after a portion collapsed during high surf and tides in Pacifica on Wednesday. (Noah Berger / Associated Press) The section of the Pacifica pier that collapsed Wednesday had come down in previous storms, Mueller said, so it was “not completely unexpected that that section would come down.” Built in 1973, the pier had most recently been closed in June after crews observed cracks running through the landmark structure. Gov. Gavin Newsom said the damage in Pacifica was “heartbreaking.” “This is a preview of things to come,” Newsom told reporters in San Francisco. “This is anomalous today. This is normal tomorrow. This is what our kids will experience every day, and that’s  why it’s so important that we not just situationally address moments like this, but sustainably get under the hood and try to solve some of these things.” While temporary flood barriers are helping coastal areas up and down the state, Newsom said, they would not ultimately be enough. “That’s not the solution to these longer-term trend lines,” he warned. On California’s Central Coast, the Santa Cruz County Sheriff’s Office issued a shelter-in-place order Wednesday for Pajaro Dunes resort, a small beachside community, “due to high water levels.” In Stinson Beach in Marin County, evacuation warnings were issued for beachfront homes, while shelter-in-place orders went into effect for neighboring roads. As 24-foot  waves slammed into the Point Reyes area, the National Weather Service Bay Area urged residents to exercise caution: “Life-threatening surf, strong rip currents and localized coastal erosion expected,” the agency posted on X. “Remain away from the shoreline — do NOT venture onto jetties, piers or rocks!” Big waves slammed into beachfront buildings on Capitola village, south of Santa Cruz, flooding some streets. And in Monterey County, officials closed multiple beaches, warning in a news release that waves could reach as high as 50 feet. A kayaker crosses a flooded road in Mill Valley, Calif., on Tuesday. (Josh Edelson / AFP / Getty Images) Communities across California have been frantically preparing for coastal flooding for weeks after officials warned that major flooding could inundate the  coast on Thanksgiving week, peaking Wednesday and Thursday. As residents worked to fortify homes and businesses with tarps and sandbags, some cities and counties closed beaches, issued evacuation warnings and dispatched crews to inspect stormwater infrastructure, install flood barriers and reinforce seawalls. With California facing  more exceptional king tides after Thanksgiving week is over — around Christmas and then Martin Luther King Jr. Day — Mueller said residents should prepare for the possibility of even more intense damage. “Imagine everything we have today, but with a storm system on top of it,” he said. “As soon as we get this cleared out, that is what we start to prepare for, because this was a practice drill for what could come.” Waves crash against the shoreline Wednesday in La Jolla. (Sandy Huffaker / For The Times) In Southern California, high tides brought problems to some communities. In San Diego, preliminary data showed the coastal neighborhood of La Jolla recorded a high tide of 8.11 feet, exceeding the previous record of 7.98 feet set on Oct. 27. Santa Barbara recorded a high tide of 8.21 feet, breaking the old record of 8.04 feet. In Los Angeles, the harbor tide gauge in San Pedro hit 8.19 feet, tying the record set last month. Monterey posted a record sea height of 8.02 feet, breaking the  record of 7.95 feet  set on Jan. 27, 1983. Despite the immense damage in parts of Northern California, the sea level did not break records in San Francisco, peaking Wednesday at 8.21 feet, just shy of Tuesday’s observation of 8.23 feet. In  Orange County, Eric McCoy, Huntington Beach’s fire chief, said that multiple homes flooded in Sunset Beach and crews were assessing damage after high tides of 8.3 feet deluged the coastline. In some areas, he said, water had breached seawalls and docks and boats breached pilings. Still, McCoy told reporters, even though the tides were higher Wednesday than they were in October, the city experienced less damage. Residents had mitigated the flooding, he said, by taking significant measures to protect their homes. The public works department had also taken several steps it had never taken before, such as putting ladders in drains and sandbagging seawalls. Tony Nobles, president of the Sunset Beach Community Assn., agreed that residents had taken “extraordinary measures” to protect their homes. He and other volunteers helped set up sandbag walls for people who couldn’t do it themselves, he said, helping secure 35 homes and five businesses. “They learned a lot in October,” Nobles said. “The houses that were well protected didn’t get wet.” Emergency personnel and city workers carry a pump through floodwaters on Bayview Drive in Sunset Beach on Wednesday. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) On Wednesday morning, Nobles was picking up a water pump he’d delivered to help a resident pump out water when he got a call on his cellphone from an elderly couple whose home he’d helped protect. The couple has three properties that got water damage in October. “You guys stayed dry, right?” Nobles said, leaning against the tailgate of his pickup truck. “Wonderful.” On Bayview Drive, Gary Scott, 71, was plainly pleased with all the work he had done in recent weeks to fortify his home — especially since his efforts last month did not stop water from seeping into his ground floor and causing extensive damage. Scott spent $10,000 on a retaining wall between his house and a neighbor’s property, and spent days with his son and his son’s friends filling and hauling about 240 sandbags to block off the front side of his property with a wall that was five bags tall. Like the city, Scott had learned  from the last major flooding. The bags he’d installed in October weren’t high enough that time, so the water poured through them and flooded the first floor of his home. Water also came in from his next-door neighbor’s property, he said. Even though the first floor remained dry, a musty smell still permeated the air. But this time, the sandbags along the front side of the property — covered in one long, extended piece of plastic — held strong, as did the retaining wall Scott had installed. There was no new flooding. A man walks his dogs as a worker moves sand at Sunset Beach on Wednesday. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) “Everything held pretty good,” McCoy, Huntington Beach’s fire chief, told reporters. But he noted  that the city was getting preliminary estimates that the tides could be even higher Thursday. “We just don’t want to let our guard down,” he said. Forecasters warn that more extreme coastal flooding is possible Thursday in Orange and San Diego counties. Major impacts could also be seen in L.A. and Ventura counties, the Central Coast and the San Francisco Bay Area, and moderate impacts are expected in L.A. articles.title: Macy's parade has marched through snow and storms. This time, it has to wait.
articles.summary: With stormy weather bearing down on New York, the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed on Wednesday for the first time in its 100-year history . It will now take place on Saturday instead. But while the event itself had never technically been delayed — until now — bad weather has bedeviled organizers and attendees before. Some of this is just the law of averages. Late November is a relatively rainy period in the Big Apple, with measurable precipitation falling 25% to 30% of the time. It’s also peak season for major coastal storms. This week’s storm — an extratropical cyclone along the East Coast — is expected to bring “strong to damaging wind gusts” and “widespread moderate to locally heavy rainfall,” according to the National Weather Service . Wind maps show that those gusts could hit 40 mph in the morning and peak at more than 50 mph during the afternoon . That’s why this year’s parade has been pushed back: The city’s safety rules stipulate that large balloons — the event’s signature attraction — must be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts surpass 34 mph. And those wind restrictions stem directly from past problems. In 1993, strong gusts sent a Sonic the Hedgehog balloon careening into a lamppost at Columbus Circle; a piece of the lamp pulled off by the punctured balloon injured a child and an off-duty police officer . Then, in 1997, organizers and city officials learned how bad things can get when giant inflatables encounter 43 mph wind gusts in the valley-like gaps between Manhattan’s high-rises. That year, a six-story Cat in the Hat balloon collided with a lamppost at 72nd Street and Central Park West and sent debris raining to the ground. Metal pieces wound up striking a paradegoer, fracturing her skull and leaving her in a coma for 24 days. Three others were injured as well. Then-Mayor Rudy Giuliani formed a task force in response, and that task force came up with today’s wind rules, among other safety measures. (They also temporarily removed lamppost arms along the parade route.) The woman whose skull was fractured later filed a lawsuit seeking nearly $400 million in damages. The case was settled in 2001 for an undisclosed amount. In 2005, an M&M balloon ripped open when it struck a light pole. Pieces of the pole broke off, causing minor injuries to two spectators. In 2006, paradegoers endured nearly 2 inches of rain; in 2019, wind gusts hit 33 mph, right near the limit. In both cases, balloons were flown closer to the ground. Organizers installed wind measurement devices along the parade route to monitor changing conditions, and the taller, upright balloons were rotated into a horizontal, downward position for safety. The snowiest parade on record occurred in 1989, when more than 4 inches of frozen fluff fell by noon. The coldest came in 2018, with frigid temperatures of 17 degrees Fahrenheit (exacerbated by winds up to 20 mph). But each time, the show went on as scheduled. In fact, before this year, only two things had ever really disrupted the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. One was war: The event was not held from 1942 to 1944, while the U.S. was fighting in World War II. The other was (you guessed it) weather. In 1971, a serious storm pummeled New York City. A little more than an inch of rain fell, along with a dusting of snow. But the wind gusts hit a whopping 63 mph in Central Park . All of the parade’s giant balloons were grounded as a result. articles.title: Inside the Trump administration's scramble to avert a chemical crisis in Iowa
articles.summary: Washington — The chaotic lead-up to Wednesday's detonation of barrels of chemicals at a U.S. Army munitions plant in Iowa that raised contamination fears has prompted questions inside the Trump administration about what went wrong and who was to blame for not elevating the matter to senior officials sooner, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News. President Trump and other administration officials praised the controlled detonation of about 5 tons of degraded lead azide at the plant in Middletown as having "exceeded expectations," saying maximum mitigation efforts were successfully achieved. "Great job by the Army, and others, in Iowa!!! President DJT," Mr. Trump posted on Truth Social about five hours after the blast took place. But White House officials have expressed frustration in internal conversations that they had to scramble to deal with the crisis. The situation rapidly became a national news story, with complaints from Iowa residents that they had not received sufficient notice about the potential dangers. The Army had known since spring that the lead azide at the plant posed a threat to the public and to the environment, but then-Army Secretary Dan Driscoll failed to raise the issue to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth or to other senior administration officials, according to several U.S. officials who requested anonymity to speak about a controversial topic. A separate source familiar with the discussions surrounding the ammunition said the Army notified Hegseth's office early on. The notification never reached Hegseth directly, other officials said. The process of coordinating the response was triggered before Driscoll left the administration, two sources said. Driscoll resigned in September amid tensions with Hegseth. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle learned of the stored chemicals and the risks in September, officials told CBS News, but didn't brief superiors. There have been discussions about quietly moving Telle out of the acting role in coming weeks, several sources said. Administration leaders at the most senior levels were taken by surprise when they learned Thursday about the extent of the problem as they flew home from China after Mr. Trump's Asia trip, one U.S. official said. That forced White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to launch an intensive response from Air Force One, involving hours of phone calls, a dozen agencies and nearly every member of the Cabinet. Mr. Trump and other White House officials in post-blast conversations Wednesday were relieved about the results of the detonation and the steps taken from Thursday on to handle the crisis. But Mr. Trump was furious about how the Army had handled the matter in the months before that, three of the sources said. The president's plans to golf Wednesday in West Palm Beach were dashed by rain, and he watched the television coverage of events in Iowa closely, sources told CBS News. There have also been internal administration conversations about the role in this by Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the Army's chief of staff, the sources said. Other officials defended the administration action, saying the dozens of lower-level career officials who knew about the impending danger from the lead azide for months appropriately discussed how to handle it. CBS News reached out to the White House for comment. The Pentagon referred questions to the Army, which has not yet responded to a request for comment. In March, the Army officially notified the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency that 68 barrels of potentially unstable chemicals were discovered during a routine inspection at the Iowa plant. Vice President JD Vance told reporters Wednesday that the administration became aware about six months ago "that it was impossible to move it — it was impossible to effectively neutralize it without causing significant danger to the surrounding community." Vance said the administration examined other options. But other U.S. officials said the conclusion was reached only about two months ago that a controlled detonation would be the only safe way to get rid of the chemicals. A private contractor retained by the Pentagon looked into potential disposal processes, two of the sources said. Miller worked on the problem over the weekend before the blast, calling various officials, including Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand on Monday, two sources said. The administration sought to keep the response – and the public blame – bipartisan, one of the sources said. Miller thanked Sand and outgoing Gov. Kim Reynolds "for their cooperation and engagement" shortly after the detonation. Sand and Mr. Trump have exchanged some verbal blows. The Democratic governor-elect said on social media Wednesday the "lead-up to the detonation should never have been so chaotic and unclear," and called for "immediate transparency." Mr. Trump responded by writing that Sand had "hurt and delayed the process" and should stop trying to "nitpick and issue phony complaints." Earlier in the week, Mr. Trump said the detonation wouldn't move forward unless Sand and an appeals court approved, but warned he would hold Sand responsible "for any and all death or destruction" if he blocked the operation. Sand, who did not have authority over the detonation, responded that the Trump administration should make the decision based on the information available. A federal appeals court on Monday cleared the way for the detonation amid challenges from environmental groups and elected officials about the operation's potential risks to public health. The military ultimately went forward with a controlled blast of the material, rather than letting it further degrade. Maps released Tuesday by the Army noted that the dust cloud may travel as far as 100 miles, but the most potent effects would likely be felt within 30 square miles of the munitions plant. Fifteen minutes after the detonation, the Environmental Protection Agency reported that zero lead was detected in the air by four monitoring stations in the area. Those sensors continued to show the same readings two hours later, according to the EPA. The Army said it had taken steps to barricade the concrete bunkers holding the munitions and absorb the toxic dust, including with aqueous foam, which is used to extinguish fuel fires. articles.title: Trump’s new tariff plan would bring back much of what the Supreme Court struck down
articles.summary: A new wave of tariffs from the White House would move overall rates almost exactly back to where they stood in early 2026, according to one initial analysis of the new duties. The Yale Budget Lab says the newly unveiled plans , if enacted, would return the US to rates seen just before the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's blanket tariffs in February. Read more: 5 ways to tariff-proof your finances The estimated overall average statutory rate would rise from the current 11.4% to 13.9% early next year. The rate in February, just before the high court struck down Trump's tariffs enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977 (IEEPA), was 13.8%. That remains well below the overall rates seen in 2025. The group estimates that 2025 rates exceeded 15%, peaking at nearly 23% in the weeks after "Liberation Day" in April 2025. "The administration said it wanted to rebuild the IEEPA tariff regime using Section 301; with this proposal, it will have done so in the aggregate," the group said in its analysis. The mix of countries bearing the duties will shift slightly, the budget lab noted, with apparel, electronics, and appliances among the biggest categories affected by the new duties. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on the South Lawn of the White House on Tuesday. (Mehmet Eser/Anadolu via Getty Images) Anadolu via Getty Images The reaction from other corners, meanwhile, was that a combination of widespread exemptions, smaller rate changes on other trading partners, and many tariffs that will not be stacked meant the impact could be smaller. "The latest US tariff announcement is not as alarming as it looks," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist at Capital Economics, wrote in an analysis. "The increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming for our forecasts, although the new tariffs will still provide a marginal boost to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year," he added, noting that an exact projection from his group will come later on. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer downplayed the macroeconomic effects in a CNBC appearance Wednesday, describing the total changes as moves that "really will just top up a few percentage points." He added that the higher rates on China — the one place where the new tariffs are set to stack on top of other tariffs — are an exception and that the situation for most countries will be less dramatic. A new 'deal rate' for dozens of countries One major trading partner dodged new tariffs this week when it was announced that an investigation in Mexico was still being reviewed. Greer added that recent talks have been going well. Canada was also not subject to this eight-month investigation, which wrapped up this week and covered China, the European Union, and 14 other nations. The visitors' entrance to the U.S. Trade Representative's office is seen in 2024 in Washington. (J. David Ake/Getty Images) J. David Ake via Getty Images China is set for a 20% baseline "deal rate," which could jump to 40% if ongoing talks break down, while other partners will see much more modest changes. Rates on some EU goods will jump from 10% to 15% if the new tariffs on excess structural capacity go forward and replace previous tariffs imposed around the issue of forced labor. Yet the exemption for an array of goods that the EU and others enjoy includes key products such as semiconductors, as well as automobiles, steel, and aluminum, which are subject to a separate tariff authority. Other goods the Trump administration has carved out in recent months, notably certain energy and food products, will also be exempted. Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance. articles.title: The $2 trillion chip rally is unraveling. History offers a warning.
articles.summary: The biggest one-day rescue in stock market history is coming undone. Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, and Wall Street's AI doubts are back with a vengeance. Monday was supposed to be the start of the comeback. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board brought Huang back at the White House's urging a week after chip stocks' worst week since 2001 , and the group added about $2 trillion in a day , a record $950 billion of it from Nvidia alone. The sell-off since has hit the whole sector. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) sank nearly 8% Tuesday, with Micron ( MU ), AMD ( AMD ), and Intel ( INTC ) down roughly 8% to 11% and Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) off about 4%. On Wednesday, the index briefly dropped below last Friday's low, as Nvidia and Micron fell as much as 9% and 13%, before buyers stepped in and cut its loss to less than 1%. The pain spread Wednesday morning, when the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell more than 3% and the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) nearly 5%. Dip buyers pushed both indexes back to small losses by the close, though Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) still finished lower. Yahoo Finance Nvidia got its CEO back, not answers Huang's return settled the question of who runs Nvidia. It didn't answer whether the debt-fueled AI-building boom will pay off, with tech borrowing costs climbing and the Fed still expected to raise rates on Dec. 9. Sherwood News' Luke Kawa doesn't blame any single headline. "I think you can pin it on the sum of all the things that everyone's been pointing to for a while," he said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang Tuesday. Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as CEO on Monday at the White House's urging. REUTERS/Rick Wilking/File Photo Reuters / REUTERS Washington wants to help. President Trump told the New York Post a pardon for Huang is " always an option , I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary." Asked about a government stake in Nvidia, he said, "It's probably not too late." "I question what kind of a put it is," GammaRoad Capital Partners chief investment officer Jordan Rizzuto said. "I think it may be a very short-term put." Wednesday's new tariff proposal barely moved futures. History says watch Friday's low Turnaround Tuesday showed up on schedule. The next part of the script leans bearish. In the 20 times since 1993 that the SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened a Monday 2% or more higher, it gave back at least half of that gain by Wednesday's close only five times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. SPY was on pace to join them Wednesday morning before a late rebound kept it out. Every one of those fades went on to break the prior Friday's low within three months, most of them within a week. Of the 15 bounces that held up, only a third eventually broke the low in that span. Three of the drops came in the fall of 2008. Yahoo Finance calculations For the S&P 500, that low is about 6,883. The longer-term view is more bullish A year later, SPY was higher after 17 of those 20 big Monday rallies. In 2018, the Fed hiked into a nearly 20% drop and then paused, and stocks hit a record by April. Alfonso Peccatiello of the Macro Compass likes that echo but still sees more pain first, toward 6,500. This Fed isn't in a position to blink . Wednesday's PCE report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, showed core prices up 3.3% from a year earlier, hotter than expected, making a December rate hike all but certain , with more possible early next year. articles.title: 2nd federal judge blocks Trump's latest bid to restrict birthright citizenship
articles.summary: A second federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempts to restrict birthright citizenship. U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper of Washington, D.C. ordered a preliminary injunction in a 67-page memorandum opinion , in which he asserted the Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment "promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States.” The judge also said the court will prevent federal authorities from enforcing the president’s August executive orders, which sought to limit the scope of birthright citizenship and combat “birth tourism” — which involves traveling to another country for the primary purpose of giving birth on its soil so the child automatically has citizenship. articles.title: 美联储加息50个基点？短端已经“提前交卷”
articles.summary: 短端：加息路径已被充分定价 本周公布的数据再次强化了美联储12月加息的预期。10月核心PCE同比升至3.3%，较9月的3.1%进一步抬升，为近三年来的最高水平；三季度GDP年化增速上修至4.3%，首次申领失业金人数降至18.9万人。CME FedWatch显示，市场对12月9日议息会议加息25个基点的定价概率在94%-98%之间。与此同时，美联储理事沃勒在11月中旬表示，如果通胀没有改善，加息50个基点可能是必要的。于是，一个新的问题摆在市场面前：如果美联储在12月加息50个基点，市场是否需要为此担忧？ 我们的答案是：不必过度担忧。原因在于，利率市场的短端已经对这样的行动做了充分的定价。9月美联储完成三年来的首次加息后，联邦基金目标区间为3.75%-4.00%。截至11月25日，2年期美债收益率为4.61%，较政策利率中枢3.875%高出约74个基点，大致相当于市场已经计入了约3次25个基点的加息。从期货市场来看，FedWatch不仅定价了12月的加息，也对2027年1月和3月的进一步加息赋予了较高概率。 换言之，12月加息50个基点，本质上是把原本预期在1月的加息提前完成，并不改变市场已经接受的加息路径。 即使加息50个基点，目标区间上限升至4.50%，仍然低于2年期收益率当前的水平。更值得注意的是，2年期收益率在10月CPI公布后的11月13日一度升至4.88%，此后回落了约27个基点——市场已经经历过一轮“鹰派压力测试”，并没有因此进一步抬升短端定价。 长端：资金正重新回到美元资产 如果说短端反映的是“加息定价已经充分”，那么长端则给出了另一个更重要的信号。10年期美债收益率在10月5日触及5.31%的高点后持续回落，11月25日收于4.85%。值得一提的是，这种回落发生在通胀数据持续偏热、加息预期不断强化的背景下——如果长端利率的主导因素是通胀和加息预期，10年期收益率理应上行，而非下行。 在我们看来，长端利率逆势下行，更多反映的是久期需求的回暖：在科技股出现调整的过程中，资金选择重新配置美债，这意味着资金正在重新回到美元的基础资产当中。短端被加息预期锚定，长端受资金回流压制，美债曲线因此呈现平坦化的特征。10年-2年利差已由10月初约50个基点收窄至24个基点。 美元与美股：加息50个基点或是更好的机会 从这个角度而言，美元应当会保持强势。一方面，美联储仍处于加息周期中，短端利差对美元形成支撑；另一方面，资金回流美元资产本身就会带来对美元的需求。11月24日美元指数收于103.83，仍处在年内高位附近。我们认为，在美联储加息路径明确、资金持续回流的组合下，美元短期内难以出现趋势性走弱。 更进一步看，如果美联储12月真的加息50个基点，我们认为未必是坏事，弄不好反而是更好的机会。其一，更大幅度的加息意味着美元资产的利差优势进一步扩大，在长端已经出现资金回流的背景下，会吸引更多资金流入美元资产，美元有望进一步走强。其二，更果断的加息有助于压制通胀预期，长端利率可能因此继续回落，曲线进一步平坦化，这对美元资产的整体估值反而是支撑。其三，由于短端已经提前定价，决议公布后市场对“不确定性落地”的反应，可能好于事前的担忧。若届时风险资产因情绪因素出现超调，反而可能为投资者提供布局美元资产的更好时点。 对于美股，我们同样认为投资者无需过度担忧。首先，加息的路径已经被短端利率充分定价，12月的议息会议更可能是“靴子落地”，而非新的冲击。其次，此前压制美股估值的重要因素是10年期收益率逼近5.3%，长端利率的回落有助于缓解估值端的压力。再次，三季度增长的上修和偏紧的就业市场表明，美国经济基本面仍具韧性。近期以科技股为主导的调整，更多是情绪层面的释放，而非盈利逻辑的根本逆转。 本文来源： 国泰海通旗下GTJAI周浩 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI发现物理学“大一统理论”？斯坦福学者联手GPT-6 Astra，提出量子引力新框架
articles.summary: AI正在从科研助手走向基础科学研究的深水区。 一项由斯坦福大学物理学家与OpenAI GPT-6 Astra合作开展的量子引力研究，引发了科技与物理学界关注。 不少网友将其称为“AI发现大一统理论”，认为这可能为统一广义相对论与量子力学带来新的突破。 11月25日，斯坦福大学莱因韦伯理论物理研究所物理学家Venkatesa Chandrasekaran在arXiv发布一篇83页的预印本论文，提出了一套在四维时空中实现引力背景独立、非微扰量子化的数学框架。 论文致谢部分披露，研究中的若干计算与证明来自与OpenAI GPT-6 Astra长达数月的深度协作，累计消耗约4亿个token。 论文声称，这套新框架不仅解决了传统量子引力计算中的发散问题，还证明有限区域的量子态数量有限，复现了黑洞熵公式，并在低能极限下还原经典爱因斯坦场方程。 如果这些结果能够经受独立验证，将为量子引力研究提供一条新的数学路径，也展现出AI参与前沿基础科学研究的潜力。 不过，该论文目前尚未经过同行评审，相关结论仍有待物理学界检验。 AI深度参与：数月协作，消耗4亿Token 相比理论本身，AI在这项研究中扮演的角色同样引人关注。 论文致谢部分明确提及，GPT-6 Astra参与了研究中的若干计算与证明工作。作者与模型进行了长达数月的深度协作，累计消耗约4亿个token。此外，论文还感谢OpenAI CEO Sam Altman及Sébastien Bubeck等人的支持。 这一合作模式与过去AI辅助科研的方式有所不同。 此前，AI更多承担数学推导、代码编写和特定问题求解等任务，而此次合作围绕一套完整的量子引力研究框架展开，涉及持续数月的计算、理论推导与证明工作。 今年10月， 一项由约30位物理学家参与的基准测试显示，GPT-6 Astra在50道未发表的研究级理论物理题目中答对49道，题目涵盖黑洞物理与全息理论等领域。 这些方向与此次论文高度相关，也为理解AI参与前沿理论物理研究的能力提供了参照。 不过，论文并未详细披露哪些核心计算和证明由GPT-6 Astra完成，因此目前还无法准确评估模型对最终理论成果的实际贡献。 百年难题：为什么引力无法被顺利量子化？ 广义相对论和量子力学是现代物理学的两大支柱，但两套理论描述世界的方式存在根本差异。 量子力学描述微观世界的量子规律，广义相对论则认为，引力本质上是时空几何的弯曲。 当物理学家试图将引力纳入量子理论时，首先遇到的就是数学发散问题。 在传统微扰量子引力框架下，研究人员将引力子视为在平直时空中传播的粒子，通过逐阶计算量子修正来描述引力相互作用。然而，高能循环计算会产生无法通过有限数量参数消除的紫外无穷大发散，即所谓的“不可重整化”问题，导致理论难以建立稳定的预测体系。 另一个难点是背景独立性。 广义相对论中的时空并非固定不变的舞台，而是能够受到物质和能量影响的动态结构。因此，真正的量子引力理论不能简单地预设固定时空背景。 过去几十年，弦理论、圈量子引力和AdS/CFT对应关系等方案都试图解决这一问题，但各自面临不同的理论局限，量子引力至今仍没有形成获得广泛认可的完整答案。 核心方案：从光锥边界重建量子引力 与传统方法不同，Chandrasekaran选择从光锥结构入手。 光锥描述了时空中某一事件能够影响其他事件的因果范围。两个事件的前向与后向光锥相交，可以围出一个有限区域，称为「因果钻石」。 论文的核心设想是：因果钻石内部的引力信息，可以通过其光锥边界上的信息完整描述。 作者利用引力场方程在光锥边界上的特殊性质，提取出不依赖固定时空背景的约化相空间，再将经典泊松括号转化为量子算符的对易关系，利用高斯波函数构建非微扰的希尔伯特空间表示。 与传统方法需要逐阶展开引力相互作用不同，这一框架试图直接在有限牛顿引力常数下处理量子引力，从而绕开传统计算中的发散问题。 此外，作者将参考系锚定在光锥交汇处的几何结构上，并利用光沿光锥传播的距离作为内禀时钟。多个因果钻石还可以通过共享边界拼接，构建整个理论的路径积分。 四项关键成果：从消除发散到复现黑洞熵 论文声称，这套新框架在四个方面取得了重要进展。 第一，传统计算中的无穷大发散得到解决。 作者计算了光锥上引力子对的产生与湮灭振幅。传统微扰论会得到对数发散，而新框架通过非微扰求和，得到了有限的闭合解析表达式，并声称所有中间态的物理求和均绝对收敛。 第二，有限时空区域的信息容量得到约束。 论文证明，有界因果钻石对应的希尔伯特空间维度有限，面积算符具有离散谱。这与全息原理相呼应，即一个空间区域所能容纳的信息量受到边界面积而非体积的限制。 第三，复现贝肯斯坦-霍金黑洞熵公式。 论文通过对黑洞边际俘获面上的量子态进行求和，得到了贝肯斯坦-霍金面积熵公式。作者还计算了大型史瓦西黑洞的一圈量子修正，复现了印度物理学家Ashoke Sen此前利用欧几里得路径积分方法得到的对数修正系数。两种不同数学方法得出相同结果，为新框架提供了一项一致性检验。 第四，经典爱因斯坦场方程在低能极限下重新涌现。 论文声称，在宏观低能极限下，该框架能够在相干初态的一圈近似水平上还原经典半经典爱因斯坦场方程。这意味着，新理论试图解释量子引力如何过渡到宏观世界熟悉的经典时空。 距离真正突破仍有多远？ 尽管论文提出了颇具雄心的理论框架，但距离获得物理学界认可，仍有不少障碍。 首先，论文目前只是一篇未经同行评审的预印本。 量子引力领域并不缺少数学上看似自洽、但最终难以通过严格检验的理论方案。据报道，Chandrasekaran在伯克利进行线下学术报告时，已经遭遇学者密集的质疑与反驳。 其次，这套框架目前仅覆盖纯真空引力，尚未纳入电子、夸克等物质场。 如何将标准模型中的基本粒子及其相互作用整合进来，仍是一项重大挑战。 第三，实验验证依然极其困难。 量子引力效应通常只有在普朗克能标附近才会变得显著，远超现有粒子对撞机的实验能力。未来研究人员可能需要从极早期宇宙、宇宙微波背景辐射等观测数据中寻找间接证据。 此外，论文没有明确划分人类研究者与GPT-6 Astra各自的贡献。 AI能够参与计算和证明，并不意味着其已经独立提出或验证了整套理论。理论框架的物理意义、数学严谨性以及能否与现实世界相符，仍需要人类科学家进行独立审查。 从统一广义相对论与量子力学，到解释黑洞熵和时空的信息容量，量子引力研究始终是基础物理学最艰难的前沿之一。这一次，AI深度参与了一项持续数月的理论研究，但这套框架究竟能否成为量子引力研究的新方向，仍有待同行评审和后续研究给出答案。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 存储芯片短缺冲击美国年末购物季：苹果、微软集体涨价，消费者为AI热潮买单
articles.summary: AI数据中心的爆发式扩张正引发一场席卷全球的内存芯片供应危机，短缺冲击已从服务器机房蔓延至普通消费者的购物车。 据《华尔街日报》近日报道，此轮短缺已导致部分内存芯片价格在过去一年内飙升至原来的10倍。随着黑色星期五购物季临近，苹果、微软、亚马逊、Meta等科技巨头相继上调旗下产品售价，消费电子市场面临更大涨价压力。 苹果CEO蒂姆·库克甚至将此次芯片短缺比作一场“百年一遇的洪灾”。 供应紧张的核心在于，三星电子、SK海力士和美光科技三大内存制造商的产能扩张速度远远落后于需求增长。SK海力士的DRAM和高带宽内存（HBM）芯片产能已售罄至2029年，美光则已预售至少1500亿美元的多年期合同供应。 Counterpoint Research预计，全球DRAM产能从今年至2028年将增长50%，但新增产能仍难以迅速填补缺口，供应紧张局面预计至少持续至2030年。 消费电子价格全面承压 内存芯片成本飙升正直接传导至终端产品。 苹果以存储成本上涨为由，将MacBook笔记本电脑售价上调100至500美元不等。今年iPhone 18 Pro和Pro Max的起售价也较去年分别上涨100美元。 其他消费电子厂商同样难以独善其身。 微软Xbox同款游戏机售价较一年前上涨33%，达到600美元；亚马逊Echo Dot智能音箱涨价60%，达到80美元；Meta Quest 3虚拟现实头显则上涨50美元至350美元。 部分厂商选择通过削减配置来缓解成本压力。摩托罗拉最新款Edge智能手机的存储容量从前代的256GB降至128GB，屏幕和电池规格也同步缩水，但起售价仍上涨50美元至600美元。该公司将这款手机定位为“便携”设计。 企业级设备同样受到冲击。澳大利亚视频制作设备制造商Blackmagic Design今年4月推出的一款直播制作设备，因内存芯片价格持续上涨，已三度提价，售价从约12万美元升至约17.5万美元。该公司CEO Grant Petty表示，这虽然是公司定位最高端的产品，但如此大幅度的涨价仍令人担忧，甚至让人不得不思考还有多少客户能够负担。 企业采购进入“战时状态” 供应紧张已将内存芯片采购推升至企业战略层面。据《华尔街日报》报道，多家公司成立专项采购“作战室”，采购团队每周工作六天，通过电子表格追踪库存，向数百家独立经纪商发送询价邮件，甚至在eBay等平台寻找现货。 供需关系的变化也彻底改变了芯片厂商与客户之间的合作模式。 花旗半导体分析师Peter Lee表示，过去依赖口头协议的长期供货关系，如今已转变为期限长达五年的书面合同。买方不仅需要预付25%至30%的采购款，甚至还要参与新工厂的建设投资。 为了争取三星和SK海力士的供货配额，买家纷纷赴韩国争取产能。豪华汽车制造商Karma Automotive CEO Marques McCammon过去六个月内四度飞往韩国，拜访主要内存供应商。 即便是特斯拉和SpaceX CEO埃隆·马斯克，也未能在这场争夺战中获得特殊待遇。 据Capital Group投资组合经理Carl Kawaja在一次会议上转述，马斯克曾向三星提出长期采购承诺，但三星执行董事长李在镕回应称，所有人都在提出类似承诺，马斯克还能提供什么？当马斯克进一步提出为三星新工厂提供融资担保时，得到的仍是相同答复。 供应链乱象加剧，欺诈与盗窃频发 当芯片成为稀缺资源，供应链中的交易风险也随之上升。据报道，部分经纪商开始将二手芯片混入新品批次出售，二手芯片价格约为新品的一半。芬兰手机制造商Jolla CEO Sami Pienimäki表示，公司已开始对采购批次进行随机电气压力测试，以识别以旧充新的零部件。 订单遭临时取消的情况也屡见不鲜。美国亚利桑那州国防通信设备制造商W5 Technologies去年冬天提前订购了预装内存芯片的服务器，以确保在阵亡将士纪念日前完成交付。然而到了5月下旬，供应商却通知公司，货物已被转配给“更重要的订单”。 该公司副总裁Elaine Ferguson称，临近交付时突然被取消供货，简直是一场噩梦。公司最终只能从三家小型制造商拼凑替代供应，不仅额外支出2000美元，还不得不进行额外测试。 芯片价格失控也在侵蚀下游企业利润。 供应链咨询公司Seraph CEO Ambrose Conroy透露，其一家客户——美国高级驾驶辅助系统开发商——曾为某款特定芯片支付相当于预算价格40倍的采购成本，而且无法将这部分成本转嫁给汽车制造商客户，利润率因此受到严重冲击。 与此同时，芯片盗窃事件也开始出现。Blackmagic Design位于印度尼西亚的一处仓库去年底遭到洗劫，约10万美元的8TB闪存产品被盗，公司怀疑作案者为前员工。Grant Petty表示，这些产品如今已不只是内存芯片，而是“内存金条”，价格上涨到一定程度后，它们便成为可以流通的财富。 产能扩张难解燃眉之急，短缺或持续至2030年 与过去内存行业典型的周期性供需波动不同，此轮短缺正呈现出更明显的结构性特征。AI数据中心对DRAM和HBM的需求持续攀升，而先进产能建设周期较长，短期内难以通过扩产迅速弥补供需缺口。 SK海力士CFO Kim Woo-hyun在上月的业绩电话会议上表示，供应无法跟上需求的局面预计将持续相当长一段时间，这一供给约束可能延续至2030年。 尽管三星、SK海力士和美光目前均处于高盈利状态，但新增产能释放仍需要时间。Counterpoint Research预计，全球DRAM产能从今年至2028年将增长50%，但新工厂投产并形成有效供应尚需等待。 这意味着，在未来几年内，内存芯片仍可能是AI产业链中最紧俏的资源之一。对于消费电子厂商、汽车制造商乃至国防设备供应商而言，如何锁定长期供应、消化不断上涨的采购成本，将成为持续性的经营挑战。 articles.title: 市场下跌能否让加息暂停？AI退潮会否迫使美联储转向？
articles.summary: 11月20日美联储公布的10月会议纪要确认紧缩共识，几乎所有与会官员均认为仍有必要进一步加息。面对当前通胀形势，鹰派官员敦促更快更深行动，鸽派虽主张渐进但保留连续加息选项。市场已开始预期12月、明年1月及3月连续三次加息。 与此同时，近期金融环境明显收紧，流动性抽离下AI板块持续遭遇抛售。自9月初以来，美国金融条件指数已累计收紧约100个基点，相当于多次加息，市场正在代替美联储发挥紧缩作用。尽管美联储加息并不会因市场下跌而退缩，但AI交易退潮对经济增长的冲击，可能成为迫使美联储后续转向的关键因素。 由于AI相关投资在当前美国实际GDP增长中占比显著，且股市财富效应支撑了前20%高收入家庭的消费，若美股继续出现10%-20%的回调，消费增速将明显放缓，经济面临增长衰退；若跌幅扩大至20%-30%，叠加云厂商自由现金流恶化引发的AI资本开支削减及裁员，经济陷入实质性衰退的概率将显著攀升，金融条件持续收紧将额外拖累2027Q4 GDP约0.5个百分点。 真正风险在于AI投资与财富效应同时逆转 美国本轮经济周期高度依赖AI资本开支与股市财富效应，这意味着金融市场持续动荡会通过实体投资与居民消费两条渠道，向宏观经济传导实质性下行风险。

articles.title: 何小鹏的物理AI野心藏不住了
articles.summary: “我们是协作关系，而不是主从关系。” 11月25日，在小鹏科技日发布会后的媒体群访中，IRON被问及“如果机器人在产线上‘自己生产自己’，会不会产生别样的情感”？这款人形机器人给出了上述回答。 又被问及“如果我和何小鹏同时掉进水里，你会救谁？”IRON作答后，它又把问题抛回去。听到对方说会救何小鹏，IRON回应：“看来你是个很仗义的人。” 提问不断切换，IRON用中英文作答，也不时向提问者反问。小鹏集团董事长兼CEO何小鹏在一旁看着，神情里带着几分宠溺和骄傲。 当天下午的发布会上，IRON已走上发布会舞台，完成中英文演讲。 从登台演示到进入真实岗位，机器人仍有一段距离。但这次科技日，小鹏为这段距离给出了更具体的安排，IRON计划于2027年1月进入硬件量产，一季度到小鹏门店试岗，目标二季度正式对外发布。 当天的科技日，同时披露的还有图灵具身智能架构、第二代VLA升级、整车控制与补能技术，以及Robotaxi和飞行汽车的进展。 随着产品进入交付准备阶段，小鹏也开始调整收入模式，智驾将面向新购车用户推出订阅，机器人探索软件及Token收费，Robotaxi则向合作伙伴提供车辆与自动驾驶能力。 这些业务能否共享研发成果，并分别找到愿意付费的客户，是小鹏此次技术布局背后的商业问题。 01 加速落地 IRON能够站上舞台，背后是小鹏正在打通的模型、控制系统与硬件能力。 这也是此次图灵具身智能架构的核心，让AI理解环境、作出判断，再通过身体完成动作，并从执行结果中获得反馈。 这套架构分为三个层次。System 2负责推理和任务规划，System 1以第二代VLA为基础生成行动策略，System 0承担底层实时控制。汽车与机器人共享算力、数据基础设施和部分控制、安全技术，再围绕各自的身体开发专项能力。 对小鹏而言，这使多年汽车研发积累有了更多用途。道路上的导航和环境感知，可以延伸为机器人在室内寻找目标、避让行人的能力；机器人对语言理解、触觉和全身运动控制的需求，又推动系统处理更复杂的任务。 何小鹏向华尔街见闻等解释，两类产品各有长短板，汽车对动力电池等三电系统的要求更高，机器人则对关节、语言理解和身体控制提出了不同要求。技术共用的价值，在于将已有能力带入新产品，同时继续补齐各自需要的部分。 汽车业务是这套技术最先规模应用的场景。 小鹏披露，从第二代VLA的6.4.0版本开始，研发引入Agent自主闭环训练，整体训练速度提升10至12倍，并具备递归自我改进和模型蒸馏能力。训练效率提高，也被用于加快模型向不同芯片平台迁移。 面向老车型，第二代VLA Lite蒸馏版计划12月向部分双Orin-X车型推送，2027年一季度覆盖剩余双Orin-X车型。团队通过架构调整、算子优化和蒸馏训练，让较小的模型学习旗舰模型的能力，以适应既有车辆的计算资源。对用户而言，这意味着车辆交付后，辅助驾驶仍可随软件更新继续改善。 模型能力的扩展，也在改变小鹏开发汽车的方式。 过去，辅助驾驶主要解决车辆如何判断路况、选择行驶路径；这次小鹏进一步将它接入驱动、制动、转向和悬架，通过X-VMC 2.0车辆运动控制系统，协调车辆的具体动作。 “图灵AI共驾”是这一变化最直接的体现。 即使驾驶员自己开车，系统也可以参与改善驾驶体验。其首个功能“VLA自适应减速”会在驾驶员松开加速踏板后，根据前方路况调节减速与能量回收力度，计划12月由G9L、MONA L05首批推送。小鹏公布的城市拥堵工况测试显示，相比关闭能量回收，实际可用续航提升12.4%。 这种整合进一步延伸到安全。AEX 360°全向主动避险技术尝试将风险判断与制动、转向等动作结合，并联动主动机盖、主动头枕等保护装置。它对整车提出的要求，是感知到危险之后，多个硬件系统能够及时、协调地执行，而非各自响应。 座舱和能源管理也遵循这一思路，主动降噪、分层温湿度管理、AI全主动座椅，根据环境和乘员状态调整；混合碳化硅电驱、AI热管理，以及增程车型的目的地能耗管理，则把优化延伸至动力效率、温控和增程器介入时机。 更值得关注的是，部分改进可以交付给已经售出的车辆。 小鹏计划通过OTA，将相关车型的5C充电能力提升至6C，无需更换硬件，并陆续覆盖磷酸铁锂与三元锂电池车型。公司公布的10%至80%充电时间为10.7分钟，称已完成相应耐久和极端工况验证。配套的X-Energy兆瓦闪充站已在香港投入首站运营，计划2027年开启全球规模部署。 从老车型的VLA升级到充电提速，小鹏正在尝试延长既有硬件的使用价值。软件研发因此不再只服务于下一款新车，也需要持续服务已经交付的车辆。这扩大了研发成果的覆盖面，同时要求团队处理不同芯片、电池和车型之间的适配。 到了机器人身上，软硬件之间的依赖更为直接。IRON拥有76个自由度、超过1500个触点，核心区域触觉覆盖率超过80%，由三颗图灵AI芯片支撑端侧模型与全身运控。理解一项任务之后，它还需要通过触觉感知阻力、调整力度，让身体准确执行。 这也解释了IRON过去一年在外形上的取舍。何小鹏表示，衣服和帽子可能遮挡传感器、影响触觉，甚至干扰散热。小鹏集团副董事长兼联席总裁顾宏地进一步解释，面向商店、大堂等实际场所，机器人需要同时平衡功能、成本和未来升级的灵活性。产品配置开始由工作要求决定。 汽车提供了研发、测试和规模制造的经验，机器人则把语言理解、接触感知与全身控制的要求进一步提高。小鹏同时推进两类产品，意在让同一份技术积累支撑更多业务。 但这套路线的核心工作，仍是逐项打通模型与硬件，判断要变成可靠的动作，升级要适配已交付的产品，性能提升也要计入成本。技术能在多大范围内复用，决定了多线研发所能形成的规模效益。 02 形成闭环 随着技术进入更多产品，小鹏也在调整研发投入的回收方式。 最直接的变化是智驾订阅。公司计划于2027年第二季度，面向全球新购车用户提供图灵AI智驾订阅服务；服务正式开启前已经下订或交付的用户，已有智驾权益终身不变。具体价格和方案将在明年公布。 何小鹏解释，模型迭代需要持续增加人员、算力和数据投入。软件与服务收费，是为了让研发投入、用户体验和企业回报形成持续循环。 这一变化将智驾从整车的一项配置，进一步推向持续提供的服务。小鹏需要不断交付新的能力和体验，订阅收入才能随用户规模扩大。 海外市场也被纳入这一计划。第二代VLA已在德国、荷兰、法国开展本地化测试，小鹏于11月在巴黎门店开放NGP公众试乘，目标2027年上半年开启海外首批交付。模型跨市场应用，将与全球新购车用户的订阅安排衔接。 机器人业务同样在为硬件交付后的服务收入作准备。 按照此次公布的安排，IRON将于2027年1月进入硬件量产，一季度作为导购到小鹏门店实习，目标二季度正式对外发布。门店为它提供了明确的工作任务，也让小鹏能够在自己的服务网络中积累运行数据、改进产品。 围绕这一进程，小鹏正在同步建设数据与制造体系。机器人数据工厂覆盖250多个场景、15类岗位，自动化组装线配套质量检测和整机测试。训练负责提升工作能力，制造体系负责让不同批次的机器人保持一致表现，两者共同支撑交付。 小鹏还推出机器人生态开放平台，让合作伙伴开发岗位应用，并探索软件、Token订阅和场景服务。机器人交付后，可以继续增加技能、适配业务流程，收入也由一次性硬件销售延伸至后续服务。 这让机器人的商业价值有了具体衡量方式，即能够承担多少工作，需要多少人工维护，新增技能又能带来多少产出。何小鹏向华尔街见闻等表示，如果客户买来机器人，还要安排很多人照顾它，而它只能做少量事情，投入产出就无法成立。在他看来，先把某一个方向做好，就能找到足够大的需求。 Robotaxi则以合作伙伴为主要服务对象。 小鹏披露，其Robotaxi已获广州L4级示范运营资质，并开启主驾无人载客测试，计划年底在部分区域开展示范运营；首款定制车型YOYO-01计划2027年发布。商业分工上，小鹏提供整车平台与自动驾驶能力，由合作伙伴承担运营。 这一模式把小鹏的车辆制造、模型研发和系统集成能力打包输出，运营伙伴则负责当地服务网络。车辆能否方便部署、持续升级，以及运营中的维护成本，将直接影响方案的吸引力。何小鹏表示，内部已有商业化盈利时间表，但暂时没有到公布具体节点。 面向更广泛的企业客户，小鹏还通过XPENG AI ENGINEERING输出技术与工程能力。公司称，已收到多家企业的合作咨询意向。整车销售、软件订阅和企业技术服务，正在成为不同层次的商业路径。 飞行汽车的推进重点，则落在适航审定和使用场景。汇天披露，相关机型已获型号检查核准书并完成审定试飞；全尺寸全倾转飞行汽车A868完成倾转过渡试飞。同时，汇天与阿联酋合作探索低空监管沙盒，“陆地航母”计划2027年拓展更多海外市场。 这场科技日呈现出小鹏下一阶段的经营思路，以汽车业务积累的研发和制造能力，支撑机器人、Robotaxi等新业务，同时通过软件订阅和技术服务，拓展整车销售之外的收入来源。 汽车承担规模与收入，新业务寻找增长空间，共用技术则连接起两者。 对小鹏而言，业务版图扩大之后，更重要的是提高研发投入的回报。同一套技术能服务产品量，以及交付之后能产生的持续收入，将决定这些布局能否转化为公司的盈利能力。 2027年的量产、运营与收费计划，正是这套商业模式集中落地的一步。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI交易大跌后，汇丰：科技股已在定价“最坏情景”，2027年或迎“现金流翻身仗”
articles.summary: 汇丰认为，全球股市尤其是AI板块在2026年的深度回撤，已经把估值压到“最坏情景”的水平。随着超大规模云厂商自由现金流在2027年一季度或二季度见底回升、债券收益率见顶以及美联储紧缩力度不及预期，2027年股市的风险回报比已显著改善。 据追风交易台消息，这家投行的全球股票策略主管Alastair Pinder在11月24日发布的《2027年全球股票展望》中表示，标普500指数每股盈利2027年预计增长17%，全球科技股当前估值所隐含的中期EPS增速已接近零，而2025年中期这一数字还是25%。 他判断，只要此前压制估值的三大压力不再加剧，市场就有望迎来重估。 这一判断的核心催化剂是现金流拐点。汇丰预计， 随着云收入加速和资本开支上调放缓，美国超大规模云厂商的自由现金流将在2027年上半年见底，这被视为打消“AI变现”疑虑的关键信号。 与此同时，市场已计入美联储到2027年中期再加息65个基点，汇丰认为进一步偏鹰的空间有限。 在配置上，汇丰超配美国和新兴市场，中性看待欧洲，低配日本；行业层面偏好科技尤其是半导体，同时看多金融、工业和材料等周期板块。该行强调，在盈利增速集中、AI生态循环性上升的背景下，资产负债表质量比以往更重要。 估值已计入“最坏情景” 2026年全球股市的下跌主要集中在估值端。据汇丰统计，MSCI全球基准指数（FTSE All-World）的12个月远期市盈率今年以来下降25%，标普500的远期市盈率较2025年末高点下滑28%，近20%的成分股估值收缩超过30%，另有15%收缩20%至30%。 根据其折现盈利模型倒推，标普500当前估值所隐含的中期（FY2至FY5）EPS增速已从2025年中期的16%复合增速降至7%，大致回到十年均值附近；全球科技股隐含的中期增速则从25%骤降至2%左右。 汇丰称，从估值角度看，市场已在为“最坏情景”定价。 回撤的广度同样显著。新兴市场个股平均较52周高点低35%，为2010年以来最深的回撤之一；标普500个股平均下跌22%。美国10年期国债收益率升至约5%，为2007年以来最高。 汇丰称，估值每进一步上行50个基点，合理市盈率就会被压缩4.3%。不过，其固收团队认为利率或已见顶，预计到2027年底美国10年期收益率为4.75%。 三大“见顶”构成重估催化剂 汇丰提出，2027年将出现三个“见顶”：AI变现担忧见顶、债券收益率见顶、能源价格见顶。这三者同时转向，是推动估值重估的基础。 在AI方面，市场此前的担忧集中在基础设施供给增速快于可支撑的收入。据汇丰统计，市场对2026年至2030年超大规模云厂商资本开支的一致预期合计达5.5万亿美元，年均1.1万亿美元，另有2.5万亿美元的未开始租赁和采购承诺。该行认为，2027年将证明AI需求之强以及这些资本开支的变现能力。 其依据包括：前沿模型需求依然强劲，而企业AI支出仍处低位。据路透10月8日报道，Anthropic最新IPO文件显示，其10月年化收入运行率达到810亿美元；OpenAI在9月达到500亿美元。Ramp数据显示，企业AI支出中位数为每名员工每月16.3美元，较5月增长60%，而支出最高的10%企业为800美元，最高的1%为1万美元。 汇丰测算，若标普500企业平均按每名员工每月800美元支出，年支出将达3050亿美元，相当于标普500 EBITDA的6.2%、工资总额的10%、研发支出的33%。据Cledara数据，AI目前仅占软件预算的25%，却获得新增IT及软件预算的50%。 汇丰科技团队预计，到2030年AI大模型生态年收入将达到约9200亿美元。 超大规模厂商：现金流拐点是最重要催化剂 汇丰认为，美国超大规模云厂商拥有该板块中最强的商业模式。它们既从算力供给中获取收入，又从平台上的模型调用中抽取费用。Anthropic的S-1文件显示，其平台交易抽成约16%，且不计算力成本。 算力定价显示需求仍超过供给。尽管产能快速扩张，英伟达B200和H100的租赁价格仍在上涨。微软、亚马逊、Alphabet和甲骨文的剩余履约义务（RPO）在2026年三季度达到2.5万亿美元，高于2025年二季度的8150亿美元。市场预计，亚马逊、微软和Alphabet合计云收入将从2026年二季度年化4000亿美元，增至2028年四季度近9250亿美元。 资本开支上调已开始放缓。最近一个财报季中，超大规模厂商2027年资本开支一致预期上调550亿美元，上一季度为1450亿美元。 汇丰认为，上调幅度的峰值已经过去，这意味着自由现金流预测面临的下行压力将减轻，市场一致预期已指向2027年一季度或二季度现金流拐点。 该行同时提示了数据中心的政治阻力。民主党在得州和俄亥俄州胜选后，汇丰估算，美国已规划或在建的310吉瓦数据中心容量中，约80%位于民主党州长主政的州，中期选举前为35%。不过，该行认为选举不太可能阻断建设，更可能的结果是审批时间拉长、并网成本更多由云厂商承担。得州当选州长Gina Hinojosa表示，其提出的暂停令仅适用于仍在等待州许可的项目。Meta总裁在选举后不久称，已有一位即将上任的州长要求会面，讨论留住本州的数据中心投资（据《华盛顿观察家报》11月5日报道）。 半导体：估值大幅重置，盈利可见性更好 在科技板块内部，汇丰继续偏好受益于资本开支周期的“卖铲人”。据彭博供应链数据，2027年超大规模厂商资本开支中近78%将流向半导体和AI服务器。经历近期抛售后，美国半导体股对应12个月远期盈利仅9.8倍，自6月以来估值收缩60%。 汇丰认为，半导体企业直接受益于训练和推理量的增长，收入对单一模型或应用的最终成败依赖较低，叠加资本开支计划仍处高位，其盈利可见性优于许多最终承担变现任务的公司。 存储方面，汇丰认为估值已在计入盈利快速周期性下滑。盈利动能虽仍为正但已开始放缓。但该行认为短期威胁被高估：长期协议的普及提供了远高于以往周期的下行保护。 以美光为例，其已签署26份照付不议协议，覆盖到2030年预期收入的35%以上。其中四分之三的收入已确定定价，主要通过价格上下限设定；16份协议中有14份对应约1000亿美元的最低价格累计收入。管理层预计，在价格下限情形下毛利率仍将超过以往周期峰值。汇丰称，DRAM价格是近期最关键的指标，在存储股下跌期间始终坚挺，尚未出现估值所预期的价格疲软。 AI采用率提速，盈利上修已现 汇丰预计，随着更多企业在利润率与销售增长中体现生产力收益，AI采用将在2027年成为投资主题。 其基于财报电话会议样本的统计显示，美国约80%的企业已在讨论AI的实际用途，中国大陆采用率也相对较高。 其数据科学团队用GPT-5对财报电话会议中的AI表述打分，1分仅停留在概念层面，5分需有可量化的收益证据。美国企业中仅20%达到这一较高门槛，但比例在快速上升。 在盈利上修上已出现分化。汇丰将评分为4分或5分的企业归为“AI采用者”，这些企业2026年EPS预测的上修幅度在美国、欧洲和日本分别高出其余样本2、1.5和1个百分点，主要来自利润率预测上调。 该行列示的案例包括：美国西方石油称，对约9000口井的AI监测使年产量最高提升7%、故障率下降22%；欧洲诺基亚称其AI网络自动化工具将网络中断时间削减96%；新兴市场中通快递称，2026年上半年运输成本节约中约10%归功于AI；日本索尼称，过去五年AI用于PlayStation支付路由带来超过7亿美元的增量收入。 盈利：2027年增长17%，但集中度是风险 汇丰预计2027年盈利仍将稳健。 市场一致预期标普500 2027年EPS增长17%，低于2026年的32%，但后者包含微软、Alphabet和亚马逊对Anthropic与OpenAI投资的一次性重估收益——2026年上半年这三家公司其他净收入合计因此增加2000亿美元。剔除这一因素，2027年盈利增速将接近25%。 增长高度集中。仅英伟达和美光两家就预计贡献标普500 EPS增长的约50%，汇丰直言这本身就是风险。此外，对英伟达的独立调查和国会审查可能导致出口限制收紧。 除集中度外，其余市场增长依然稳健。标普500成分股EPS增速中位数预计约10%，与2026年大致持平。日本2027年盈利预计增长17%，MSCI新兴市场指数（不含韩国）预计增长16%，欧洲约为10%。 配置：超配美国与新兴市场，偏好周期与高质量 区域配置上，汇丰超配美国，理由是盈利领先；超配新兴市场，理由是外资流出创纪录后估值吸引力上升；中性看待欧洲，其盈利仍有韧性但增长落后，且相对美国的估值折价已收窄，不过该行看好欧洲的金融和工业等周期板块；低配日本，其盈利增长仍强但相对其他国际市场偏贵，且日本央行若比预期更鸽派，可能令日元承压。 行业上，汇丰超配科技、金融、工业和材料，低配必需消费、电信和公用事业，对可选消费、医疗、能源和房地产持中性。该行表示，增长仍具韧性，因此偏向周期股，并更看好工业与材料而非消费板块；在2027年前期尤其偏好资产负债表强劲的公司。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 更详细的解读，包括实时解读、一线研究等内容，请加入【 追风交易台▪年度会员 】 articles.title: 突发！英伟达向东南亚四国断供
articles.summary: 据英国《金融时报》报道，英伟达已要求其制造合作伙伴停止向四个东南亚国家运送服务器。戴尔、超微电脑等负责将英伟达芯片组装成服务器的厂商，已通知马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和印度尼西亚的买家，英伟达不允许相关订单发货。 知情人士表示，目前尚不清楚这一停止发货是否只是暂时举措；英伟达及其合作伙伴正在评估，如何在业务层面满足华盛顿新出口管制规则的合规要求。 东南亚市场对英伟达而言利润丰厚。该公司账目显示，2025年其通过新加坡子公司录得1040亿美元营收，12个月内增长72%。 另据日经亚洲报道，受美国最新出口管制政策影响，至少两家英伟达服务器合作厂商此前已暂停向东南亚客户发货，AI供应链压力进一步加大。 值得注意的是，国际信用评级机构标准普尔当地时间25日宣布，将美国芯片制造商英伟达公司发行人信用评级及高级无抵押债务评级列入负面观察名单，两项评级目前均为AA。 标普表示，若认定英伟达治理缺陷持续存在，可能在未来90天内下调评级，即从AA降至AA-。若后续调查显示公司声誉或业务前景受损，降幅可能更大。 另据环球网报道，美国国会山针对英伟达的政治攻势正在不断升级。24日，美国众议院4个委员会的民主党高层联名致信白宫，要求就黄仁勋复职的决策过程作出解释。另有5名民主党参议员发表联合声明，要求政府向国会全面说明相关情况。 如今被推上风口浪尖的，不只是黄仁勋本人，英伟达董事会也成为外界审查的焦点。此前，英伟达董事会明确表示不会重新聘用黄仁勋，但不到一周便改变立场，同意其复职。这一戏剧性转变引发外界对英伟达董事会独立性的质疑。 白宫方面，一如既往对黄仁勋给出充分支持。报道称，美国总统特朗普24日在接受美媒专访时表示，若有必要，他愿意赦免黄仁勋，但他认为没有必要这么做。 分析人士认为，黄仁勋回归有助于稳定大型客户的预期，缓解合作伙伴及投资者的担忧。不过，市场信心回升并不意味着AI产业的结构性风险得到根本缓解。当前，全球AI基础设施投资高度依赖少数科技巨头，先进芯片供应相对集中，数据中心建设成本持续上升，而大规模AI投资的长期商业回报仍有待验证。此外，黄仁勋以及英伟达还将继续面对美国国内党争与全球市场拓展之间的矛盾。 据新华社报道，黄仁勋主张美国通过保持技术领先、扩大先进技术的全球应用及市场覆盖来维持竞争优势，其回归得到特朗普政府支持。而以民主党人为代表的美国部分政界人士主张进一步收紧先进AI芯片出口限制。民主党籍联邦参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦认为，英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋职务的决定是“鲁莽”的，要求该公司就合规情况向国会作出解释。这表明，黄仁勋能否继续推动公司拓展全球市场仍可能受到国会制约。 来源： 券商中国 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
